title: Lake Station, Indiana: Liverpool, Lake County's lost first county seat

sources.what: Liverpool platted in January 1836 by John Chapman, Frederickson and Davis at the junction of the Deep and Little Calumet rivers; streets 100 feet wide, three squares, 40 blocks, 435 lots; three days of lot sales in July 1836 brought $16,000; commissioners favored Liverpool May 11, 1839, and a frame court house was begun; a second commission chose Lake Court House (later Crown Point) June 12, 1840; 'According to Timothy Ball, the courthouse at Liverpool, which had never been entirely finished, was sold' and 'moved on a scow down the Deep and Little Calumet rivers to Blue Island, Illinois'; 'Some persons dispute the story of the removal of the court-house'; after George Earle founded Hobart the empty buildings decayed, 'Finally the arch enemy of wooden structures appeared and demanded its toll, and only ashes remained'; in 1929 the site was a small railroad junction with a station house
sources.who: John O. Bowers, 'Dream Cities of the Calumet', History of Lake County vol. 10 (Lake County Historical Association, 1929); transcribed by inportercounty.org

sources.what: Liverpool on Deep River near its junction with the Calumet; lots laid out by Davis, Frederickson and Chapman; about $16,000 of lots sold in three days in 1836; 'became the county seat of the new Lake County in 1839'; Crown Point in 1840; George Earle gave up Liverpool and founded Hobart, building a house, a grist mill and a dam; his family moved to Hobart in 1847
sources.who: T. H. Ball, Northwestern Indiana from 1800 to 1900 (1900), ch. XIX, 'Lake County's First County Seat'; transcribed by inportercounty.org

sources.what: 'Liverpool was laid out in 1836 by John Davis, Henry Frederickson and John B. Chapman'; settlers, especially from the south of the county, protested the site; commissioners in June 1840 selected Lake Court House; 'The uncompleted courthouse building at the village of Liverpool was sold and floated down the Calumet River to Blue Island, Ill., where it was used as a tavern'; George Earle, county agent, helped name Crown Point
sources.who: Richard C. Schmal, 'How Our County Seat Was Chosen', Lowell Tribune (Jan. 26, 1994), Lowell Public Library

sources.what: '1839 Liverpool was selected as the county seat, but proved an unpopular choice. 1840 June - The temporary Lake Court House became the permanent county seat... The name of the community was changed to Crown Point'
sources.who: Crown Point Community Library, historical timeline

sources.what: 'George Earle... was instrumental in having Liverpool named the county seat. After the loss of the county seat, Liverpool stopped growing. The town of Liverpool is now gone, today the area it covered is encompassed by New Chicago and the neighboring town of Lake Station'

the county seat was once on what is now the west end of Lake Station, in a section called Liverpool; in April 1852 George Earle platted a town on the site of the Michigan Central depot, continuing its name of Lake Station (citing the WPA guide)

Liverpool, the original county seat; Earle campaigned for it; courthouse sold and floated downriver to Blue Island; Earle founded Hobart; by the late 1840s two families left; 'a fire swept through the almost-empty town'; a Lake Station neighborhood on the site is named Liverpool (citing Bowers 1929 and Goodspeed 1882)
'In 1852, the city of Lake Station was platted by George Earle alongside the very first railroad in Lake County'
sources.who: South Shore Convention and Visitors Authority, Lake Station

sources.what: 'Lake Station, platted in 1852 along the Michigan Central Railroad'
sources.who: Encyclopedia of Chicago (Newberry Library), Lake Station

sources.what: Liverpool's unfinished courthouse was floated down the river to become a tavern (citing Ball, Lake County, Indiana, from 1834 to 1872); the Lake Court House was a log building
sources.who: Ted Shideler, 'The Lake County, Indiana Courthouse (1878-1971)' (2024)

sources.what: the log building at Lake Court House adopted as the court house in 1840, the 'Old Log Court House'
sources.who: T. H. Ball, Northwestern Indiana from 1800 to 1900 (1900), ch. XXXII, 'Court Houses'

beats.text: Lake County's first county seat vanished. It stood where Lake Station and New Chicago are now.
beats.label: LAKE STATION, INDIANA
beats.credit: History: T. H. Ball (1900); Town of New Chicago; Crown Point Library

beats.text: In 1836, Liverpool was laid out where Deep River meets the Little Calumet. In three days, buyers paid $16,000 for lots.
beats.credit: J. O. Bowers (1929); T. H. Ball (1900); Lowell Public Library

beats.text: In 1839, it became the county seat, and work began on a courthouse.
beats.credit: J. O. Bowers (1929); T. H. Ball (1900); Crown Point Library

beats.text: But settlers protested. In 1840, the seat moved to Lake Court House, soon renamed Crown Point.
beats.credit: Lowell Public Library; Crown Point Library; J. O. Bowers (1929)

beats.text: An early historian wrote that the unfinished courthouse was floated downriver on a scow, to Blue Island, Illinois. Others dispute it.
beats.label: THE COURTHOUSE
beats.credit: T. H. Ball, quoted by J. O. Bowers (1929); Lowell Public Library

beats.text: George Earle, who had pushed for Liverpool, went on to found Hobart, and in 1852 he laid out Lake Station.
beats.label: GEORGE EARLE
beats.credit: T. H. Ball (1900); South Shore CVA; Encyclopedia of Chicago

beats.text: Liverpool emptied, and fire took what was left. Only the name survives.
beats.label: LIVERPOOL
beats.credit: J. O. Bowers (1929); Town of New Chicago

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

end_card.pill: Liverpool: Lake County's first county seat
